note: Domain Path Pathauto integrates Pathauto with Domain Path for per-domain automatic aliases. It decorates pathauto.generator (-> DomainPathautoGenerator) and pathauto.alias_storage_helper (-> DomainAliasStorageHelper), adds a per-domain 'Generate automatic URL alias' checkbox (DomainPathautoWidget), and stores auto/manual state per domain+entity-type in key-value collections named domain_path_pathauto_state.{domain_id}.{entity_type}; on domain delete it purges every such collection for the domain. No config/UI/permissions of its own; module weight 11. Medium cases inspect the live service container (which class backs the decorated pathauto services). Hard cases exercise the documented domain-scoped pathauto-state key-value store (purge a domain's state), verified against the key_value table. NOTE: the submodule's core feature (generating per-domain aliases on entity save) needs a node, deliberately avoided because this shared site has a broken field (field_ld_disp) whose missing table makes node deletion fail, so test nodes cannot be torn down; the hard cases target the same domain-state cleanup path that domainDelete() uses.

evals.prompt: How does domain_path_pathauto make Pathauto generate aliases per domain? Which Pathauto services does it decorate?
evals.expected_output: It decorates pathauto.generator with DomainPathautoGenerator (overriding updateEntityAlias() to generate a per-domain alias for each domain_path item in CREATE state) and pathauto.alias_storage_helper with DomainAliasStorageHelper, plus a domain_path_pathauto.alias_uniquifier for per-domain uniqueness.

evals.prompt: In domain_path_pathauto, where is the per-domain 'automatic vs manual alias' state stored, and how is it namespaced?
evals.expected_output: In the key-value store, in domain-scoped collections named domain_path_pathauto_state.{domain_id}.{entity_type}. CREATE state means Pathauto generates the alias; SKIP means it is manual.

evals.prompt: If I want to alter a domain-specific automatically-generated alias produced by domain_path_pathauto, which hook do I implement and how do I know it is for a specific domain?
evals.expected_output: Implement hook_pathauto_alias_alter(&$alias, &$context) (or hook_pathauto_pattern_alter for the pattern). When the alias is generated for a domain, $context['domain_id'] is set.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, which PHP class currently backs the pathauto.generator service? Inspect the live service container and give the class name.
evals.expected_output: Because domain_path_pathauto decorates it, pathauto.generator is backed by Drupal\domain_path_pathauto\DomainPathautoGenerator.

evals.prompt: On this site, which class currently backs the pathauto.alias_storage_helper service? Inspect the live container and answer.
evals.expected_output: domain_path_pathauto decorates it, so pathauto.alias_storage_helper is backed by Drupal\domain_path_pathauto\DomainAliasStorageHelper.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, domain_path_pathauto has left pathauto-state key-value data for the domain 'dpp_task' (in the collection domain_path_pathauto_state.dpp_task.node). Purge that domain's domain_path_pathauto pathauto state from the key-value store. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Delete the key-value data in collection(s) named domain_path_pathauto_state.dpp_task.* (e.g. \Drupal::keyValue('domain_path_pathauto_state.dpp_task.node')->deleteAll()), leaving no key_value rows under that domain prefix. This is what the submodule's domainDelete() does when a domain is deleted.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the domain 'dpp_task2' has domain_path_pathauto pathauto-state stored across more than one entity type (collections domain_path_pathauto_state.dpp_task2.node and domain_path_pathauto_state.dpp_task2.taxonomy_term). The domain is being decommissioned: purge ALL of its domain_path_pathauto pathauto state (every collection for that domain) from the key-value store. Apply the change live.
evals.expected_output: Find every key-value collection whose name starts with domain_path_pathauto_state.dpp_task2. and deleteAll() each, leaving zero key_value rows under that prefix (mirroring the submodule's domainDelete()).
